name: crownlands
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: finished hand-painted landscape art for a serious historical parallel-world mobile exploration game, NOT a UI mockup. Create a very wide panoramic canvas, 3072x1024 pixels (3:1). A single continuous landscape seen from a consistent elevated oblique map perspective, readable individual buildings, painterly realism with restrained detail and subtle paper texture. Mature, beautiful, atmospheric, not photorealistic, not cartoon, not cute, not toy-like. NO text, labels, letters, numbers, UI, borders, icons, glowing markers or speech bubbles. No modern machinery, asphalt, electricity or modern vehicles. Compose EIGHT distinct landmark clusters in a strict left-to-right journey, with comfortable landscape gaps between them. The eight cluster CENTER positions as fractions of the full image are approximately (x,y): (0.065,0.54),(0.19,0.40),(0.315,0.59),(0.44,0.43),(0.565,0.60),(0.69,0.42),(0.815,0.57),(0.94,0.45). The terrain and environment must fill the entire canvas edge to edge; distant background occupies upper quarter only, near foreground occupies lower quarter. Never present eight separate panels.
KRONENLANDE. European countryside circa 1800, late summer warm afternoon, muted sage green fields, cream stone and russet tile, old forests and gentle hills. Eight landmarks in order: 1 small half-timbered Lindenweiler village with handcart; 2 old grain watermill with waterwheel at a stream and grain sacks; 3 coaching inn with courtyard, stables and horse-drawn carriage; 4 broad stone arch bridge across a modest river with tiny tollhouse; 5 Eichenhain manor farm with barns and heavy horse team; 6 Falkenau market town with stalls and carts; 7 monumental fortified city gate, roofs and towers receding behind; 8 CROWN HARBOR as grand finale: royal trading office beside cream-stone warehouses and quay, wooden loading cranes, horse teams and river barges, beautiful interaction of land and blue-green water. Last two sites on a broad river. Use European deciduous trees and hedgerows; no sky-heavy photograph.
